While the 90% confidence intervals are designed to capture the vast majority of probable outcomes under normal market conditions, certain specific risks or "black swan" events could push the asset's performance outside these bounds. These extreme scenarios might include an unexpected and severe global economic recession, a sudden geopolitical crisis escalating into conflict, unprecedented central bank policy shifts (e.g., emergency interest rate hikes or cuts), or a major technological disruption to the industry relevant to the asset.
